/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 02 October 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3148 (8)
Baltic Capesize Index: 5042 (32)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2372 (-7)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1789 (-5)
Baltic Handysize Index: 1007 (-1)
CAPESIZE
The BCI 182 5TC recovered $296 to close at $45,731. More fixtures finally emerged from Brazil, although the C3 index fell from $40.659 on Monday to $37.65 today, equating to earnings of approximately $41,814 on the China/Brazil or West Africa round voyage. In the North Atlantic, stems were fixed from Canada to China and India whilst transatlantic demand lent support. Sentiment remained firm, particularly for the second half of October and early November as the tonnage list appeared relatively balanced. In the Pacific, the C5 index climbed to $14.425 after several west Australia to Qingdao fixtures were reported at improved levels compared with the last done.

Atlantic
The Shandong De Tai (180,702 2021) was fixed for 170,000/10 Seven Islands to Qingdao 24/30 October at $48 last night. A Swissmarine TBN was fixed by Qatar Steel for 150,000/10 Seven Islands to Kandla 4/13 November at a rate in the mid/high $46s. ArcelorMittal took a vessel from Mercuria for 170,000/10 Buchanan to Qingdao 18/27 October at $36.50. The Tata Steel tender was awarded to a Bocimar vessel for 160,000/10 Acu to Ijmuiden 3/7 November at $21.50. Cosco was linked to a vessel for 170,000/10 C3 plus West Africa option for 24 October onwards loading at $37.

Asia
There was talk of FMG taking a vessel for 160,000/10 Port Hedland to Qingdao 17/18 October but the rate was not confirmed. Berge Bulk took a TBN for 170,000/10 West Australia to China 20/22 October at a rate in the mid/high $14s.
PANAMAX
Market sources reported a quieter end to the week across both basins, with the P5TC declining by $58 to close at $21,349. Activity on both the trans-Atlantic and fronthaul routes was said to lack any clear momentum, as Charterers and Owners alike appeared content to pause ahead of the weekend and reassess their respective positions for signs of future market direction. In the Pacific, sentiment was similarly subdued, with demand from Indonesia reported to have softened and North Pacific activity also easing. Australia remained the most active area of the basin, although much like in the Atlantic, many market participants were taking the opportunity to evaluate their positions rather than pursue fresh business aggressively. The Saronic Champion (93,115 2011) open Kaohsiung 9 October was said to have fixed for a minimum period of 100 days up to a maximum of 150 days at $17,750 with the scrubber benefit for the Owners, although no further information was heard.

Atlantic
The Timorsun (81,839 2016) open Rotterdam 5 October was reported to have been placed on subjects for a fronthaul with Cofco, while the scrubber-fitted Ultra Serval (81,606 202) open Amsterdam prompt was reported to have fixed, but no other details emerged.

Asia
The Shen Hua 808 (75,411 2014) open Mauban 6/7 October fixed an Indonesia to Malaysia coal stem to Kline at a rate around $19,250 to $19,500.
SUPRAMAX
As expected, a very slow day prior to the weekend, with very fews trades circulating. The 11TC average fell $62 to end the week at $22,619, which was just $40 higher than last weeks close, so a very flat week overall. The Pacific Lotus (63,206 2019) Kendari 5-10 October fixed a trip via Indonesia to Bangladesh at close to $30,000 with Panbulk, and a 2009 built 55,000-dwt open in Sohar end Oct was said to have fixed 1 year at $18,000, however there were no further details. In the Atlantic the Continent remained firm, although off the highs of last week, with an Ultra said to be offering $39,000 for scrap to the East Mediterranean against Charterers bid of $37,000. The US Gulf rates came under further pressure without sufficient new enquiry to support a lengthening tonnage list, but rates in the South held up as the opposite was true, but there was limited upside with Owners deciding to ballast from the Mediterranean rather than fix local business.
HANDYSIZE
It was a typically quiet end-of-week session, with minimal activity and little fresh information emerging. The BHSI edged down by 1 point to 1,007, while the 7TC average slipped by $30 to close at $18,117. Rates across the Continent and Mediterranean remained broadly flat, holding around previous levels. Meanwhile, the South Atlantic and US Gulf markets moved at a slow pace amid negative sentiment, with limited cargo availability and a growing tonnage list. The Pacific market saw little change in its underlying dynamics and remained broadly steady. On the period front, the Nani K (37,423 2014) open Qinzhou on 28 September was heard fixed by Lauritzen for 3 to 5 months at $18,500, and a the EB Grand (40,174 2024) open Continent in early October was heard fixed for 12 months at $18,000, although further details were lacking.

Atlantic
The Team Bravo (33,642 2012) open Barranquilla on 29 September was placed on subjects by Aries for a trip via Pascagoula to India with under-deck logs in the low $20,000s, although further details were not disclosed.

Asia
The Phoenix Nereid (29,070 2011) open Haiphong, Vietnam 6–9 October was fixed for a trip to Korea in the mid-$12,000s. The Moonbright SW (36,378 2012) open Pasir Gudang 9–12 October was placed on subjects for a trip from Australia to the Far East with alumina in the $16,000s, although further details were not disclosed. In addition, a 40,000-dwt vessel was heard fixed from CJK via Wakayama to Floro via COGH at around $21,000, with further details lacking.

Market Fundamentals
US Weekly Grain Exports

In the week to 24 September, US combined exports of corn, wheat, soy (beans and meal) and sorghum fell 0.4 Mt from the preceding week to 3.0 Mt, marking a 0.1 Mt year-on-year decrease, USDA data show. The decline was led by wheat shipments, which fell 0.6 Mt year-on-year to 0.3 Mt. In contrast, soy (beans+meal) exports rose 0.4 Mt to 1.3 Mt, while corn exports held steady at 1.4 Mt.

Trading Commentary
Cape
Cape moved sharply lower through the afternoon after a firmer morning. Oct started around 40,000, briefly reached 40,750, before falling steadily to 39,000 and later 38,750 with heavy volume. Nov reached 41,650 in the morning before easing to around 40,500–40,600. Dec traded up to 41,150 before moving back toward 40,100 late. Q4 26 firmed from 40,500 to 41,250 with substantial volume, before falling to 40,000 and later printing 40,500. CONTINUING ITS GRADUAL DECLINE, NOPAC REMAINED ONE OF THE CONTRIBUTING FACTORS BEHIND THE WIDER PACIFIC MARKET'S SOFTER PERFORMANCE. THE AUSSIE MARKET INITIALLY SHOWED HEALTHY DEMAND, WITH CHINESE AND JAPANESE CHARTERERS ACTIVE FOR COAL SHIPMENTS ACROSS THE SECOND HALF OF OCTOBER. THIS PROVIDED SOME UNDERLYING SUPPORT, AND THERE WAS A REASONABLE VOLUME OF FRESH ENQUIRY AT THE BEGINNING OF THE WEEK. HOWEVER, THE CARGO LIST DIMINISHED QUITE SIGNIFICANTLY FOLLOWING TUESDAY'S ACTIVITY, WITH MOST OF THE REMAINING REQUIREMENTS SHIFTING TOWARDS THE 20–30 OCTOBER DATES. DEMAND WAS FAIRLY EVENLY SPLIT BETWEEN INDIA AND CHINA DESTINATIONS, ALTHOUGH OVERALL VOLUMES REMAINED RELATIVELY THIN. TOWARDS THE LATTER PART OF THE WEEK, BOTH CARGO AND VESSEL COUNTS DROPPED CONSIDERABLY AS CHINESE CHARTERERS STEPPED AWAY FOR GOLDEN WEEK, LEAVING THE MARKET QUIETER AND WITH LIMITED FRESH IMPETUS. THE INDO MARKET STARTED THE WEEK ON A RELATIVELY STEADY NOTE, FOLLOWING THE EARLIER SURGE IN COAL DEMAND, WITH CONTINUED ENQUIRY FROM SOUTH CHINA HELPING MAINTAIN ACTIVITY. HOWEVER, MOMENTUM GRADUALLY EASED, AND THE MARKET BEGAN TO LAG BEHIND THE OTHER PACIFIC ROUTES AS THE WEEK PROGRESSED. FRESH STEMS WERE PRIMARILY CONCENTRATED AROUND THE FIRST AND SECOND HALF OF OCTOBER, WITH SOME REQUIREMENTS CONTINUING TO EMERGE FOR INDIA AND SOUTHEAST ASIA DESTINATIONS. BY WEDNESDAY, THE CARGO COUNT HAD STARTED TO THIN OUT, AND THE MARKET SAW CONSIDERABLY LESS FRESH ENQUIRY, PARTICULARLY FROM CHINESE CHARTERERS. THIS SLOWDOWN BECAME MORE EVIDENT ON THURSDAY, WHEN VERY LITTLE FRESH DEMAND WAS REPORTED APART FROM A HANDFUL OF STEMS. WITH TONNAGE AVAILABILITY REMAINING A FACTOR AND FEWER CHARTERERS ACTIVELY PARTICIPATING, INDO RATES FACED SOME DOWNWARD PRESSURE, ALTHOUGH ACTIVITY WAS ALSO HEAVILY DISTORTED BY THE HOLIDAY PERIOD. LOOKING AHEAD, THE PACIFIC MARKET IS LIKELY TO REMAIN SUBDUED IN THE IMMEDIATE TERM AS GOLDEN WEEK CONTINUES TO RESTRICT CHINESE PARTICIPATION, ALONGSIDE REDUCED ACTIVITY FROM OTHER KEY MARKETS. ONCE EVERYONE RETURN, THE BALANCE BETWEEN FRESH CARGO AVAILABILITY AND THE GROWING TONNAGE SUPPLY WILL BE KEY IN DETERMINING WHETHER THE MARKET CAN REGAIN SOME OF ITS LOST MOMENTUM. rows: . The Supramax and Ultramax markets across ECSA and West Africa maintained a strong footing this week, with overall rate levels remaining firm across key trade routes. However, market momentum has slowed slightly due to the Chinese National Day Golden Week holidays, which naturally tempered prompt fixture activity as vessel and cargo negotiations briefly paused. Despite the holiday induced lull, underlying support remains solid, and rate structures across both ECSA and West Africa continue to hold near their recent levels as market participants await the resumption of full trading post-holiday. This week, the Handysize US Gulf market faced a modest downward correction following the exceptionally strong conditions seen in recent weeks. With plenty of tonnage available for the first half of October coupled with cargo requirements mostly dated for mid-October onwards, we saw the bid-offer gap grow wider as Charterers have started to Owners’ willingness to adjust their rate ideas in order to secure employment. Much of the tonnage positioned in NCSA is now ballasting to North Brazil due to the lack of available cargo in the region, which will alleviate some pressure. Fixing activity remains healthy, however the levels we are seeing are sitting below that of the last done, with a TA sitting at around $23- 24,000 aps, and local runs at around $21,000 aps. The USG SMX market didn't roar back into life, after the ASBA Miami event, as some were hoping. Whilst a robust sentiment still remains, the fact is there's a lack of cargo for early October and we're seen this affect the SMX rates accordingly. We've lost a few thousand usd off most routes. FH grain runs have been hardest hit; hearing today a 63kdwt has fixed grains to Sgp/Jpn at 30,000 usd pd with some waiting days. There's still some prompt ships holding out for next week and the return of the Chinese after golden week. Expect more activity on Monday.
